a.speaker: system
a.text:
A ball hits the cloister wall. Catch. Turn. Again.
She's been at it long enough to wear a pale spot in the stone.

b.speaker: ivy
b.text:
You're from the harbor. I heard the Kettle went quiet.
That was you, wasn't it.

d.speaker: ivy
d.text:
Nothing else to do up here but listen.
I'm Ivy. Fastest feet on this hill, not that the Saints care.

e.speaker: ivy
e.text:
They say I'm not grown into patience yet.
Ninety years of the low block and they want me PATIENT.

f.speaker: ash
f.text: So play us. The Crew doesn't wait for anyone to grow.

g.speaker: ivy
g.text:
The Saints don't play outsiders. Old rule.
Unless the bell keeper vouches for you — and Alder vouches for nobody.

h.speaker: ivy
h.text:
He's by the tower. Go on. Ask him.
I want to watch him say no.

a.speaker: ivy
a.text:
Still here. Still faster than all of them.
How's the old man treating you?

a.speaker: alder
a.text:
The yard is open to walkers. The cage is not.
If you came to play, the hill has rules older than you.

b.speaker: alder
b.text:
Talk to the girl by the wall. She'll enjoy explaining them.
She finds the rules as heavy as you will.

a.speaker: ash
a.text:
Keeper Alder? I'm told you vouch for outsiders.
I'm told you never do.

b.speaker: alder
b.text:
Both true. Vouching is spending trust,
and I mind the tower's accounts carefully.

c.speaker: alder
c.text:
But you can earn a hearing. The storm took every lantern
in the yard last month. The wind up here eats plain wicks.

d.speaker: alder
d.text:
Nadia at Spicegate keeps the only storm-lanterns that survive
this hill. Bring one up the steps. Then we talk.

e.speaker: alder
e.text: It matters more than it sounds. On this hill you keep—

g.speaker: alder
g.text: Old habit. Go on, harbor kid. The steps are long.

a.speaker: ash
a.text: Alder needs a storm-lantern. For the yard.

b.speaker: nadia
b.text:
Alder. There's a name that pays on time.
He buys wicks he doesn't need, you know. Every month, forty years.

c.speaker: ash
c.text: Why would anyone buy wicks they don't need?

d.speaker: nadia
d.text:
Because somebody once told him a light's no good
if you're the only one keeping it.

e.speaker: nadia
e.text:
Here. No charge — his account's paid past both our lifetimes.
Tell him the book stays shut.

a.speaker: alder
a.text:
The steps are long. The light matters more.
Nadia's stall, down at Spicegate.

a.speaker: system
a.text:
Alder takes the lantern with both hands, like it weighs
more than it does. He hangs it at the yard gate and lights it.

b.speaker: ash
b.text: Nadia says the book stays shut.

d.speaker: alder
d.text:
The wind takes every light on this hill, harbor kid.
Somebody has to keep one on. Tonight it's you.

e.speaker: alder
e.text:
So: I vouch. The Prior will hate it, which is half the reason.
Go knock on the Cloister.

f.speaker: ash
f.text: And the tower? The door's always locked.

g.speaker: alder
g.text:
Beat the Saints and I'll show you what's under the bell.
Some things you earn the long way. That one especially.

a.speaker: alder
a.text:
The lantern's still burning. Good sign.
The Cloister is waiting on you.

a.speaker: prior
a.text:
The yard prays at dusk and plays at its own pace.
Come back vouched-for, or don't come back.

a.speaker: prior
a.text:
So Alder spent his voice on you. Forty years of silence,
broken for a harbor kid. Fine.

b.speaker: prior
b.text:
One condition of ours: Ivy starts. Against you.
Her asking, not mine. Beat patience with patience — or don't.

a.speaker: prior
a.text:
Ninety years this block has held.
We do not chase. We do not tire. We wait.

b.speaker: ivy
b.text:
And I run. Don't go easy on me, harbor.
If you win, I want it to have been true.

c.speaker: system
c.text:
THE CLOISTER — the Saints sit deep and spring Ivy on the break.
Be patient. Move them. The gaps come to those who wait.

a.speaker: prior
a.text: You chased. The block ate you. This is the lesson.

b.speaker: ivy
b.text:
Psst. They're statues till the ball moves them.
Swing it side to side. Make the old bones turn. Again.

a.speaker: prior
a.text:
...Ninety years.
Well. Every wall meets its water.

b.speaker: prior
b.text:
The Saint pin goes down the hill. Carry it evenly.
It has never once left Old Cobble. Mind that.

c.speaker: system
c.text:
PIN EARNED — THE COBBLE SAINTS
Three pins. The ladder has one rung left: Voltside.

d.speaker: ivy
d.text:
Hey. Harbor.
That was true. All of it. So — take me down the hill.

e.speaker: ash
e.text: You sure? This hill made your feet what they are.

choices.text: The harbor could use you. Come down.
Make the Prior start you first. Then come.

f.speaker: ivy
f.text:
Ha! Deal. Give me a week to say my goodbyes —
ninety years of statues, somebody's got to hug them.

g.speaker: ivy
g.text:
...You sound like Alder. Fine. One start, in the yard,
with the whole hill watching. THEN I'm coming down.

h.speaker: alder
h.text:
When you're done celebrating, harbor kid —
the tower door is open. I keep my accounts.

a.speaker: system
a.text:
Alder unlocks nothing — the door already stands open.
Inside, under the First Bell, a plaque worn smooth by thumbs:

c.speaker: system
c.text:
The bell's wheel gleams. A fresh drop of oil.
Forty years of wicks nobody needed. Somebody keeps it turning.

d.speaker: alder
d.text:
She rang this one before any of the cages had theirs.
Ask your coach who held the ladder. Or don't. Some bells rest.

a.speaker: ivy
a.text:
Packing takes a week when everything you own is one ball.
Save me a spot on the quay, harbor.

a.speaker: ivy
a.text:
The Prior posted the next yard game. My name's FIRST.
Forty years of statues and my name is first. Then I'm yours.

a.speaker: prior
a.text:
The block held ninety years. It can spare one dusk.
The girl plays with her whole chest now. Perhaps you knocked something loose.

a.speaker: alder
a.text: Three pins going home to the harbor. She'd have laughed.

c.speaker: alder
c.text: ...The lantern's burning well tonight. Play on, harbor kid.
